feed.title: al-ice.ai — AI security intelligence
feed.subtitle: Primary-source-led intelligence on AI vulnerabilities, agents, and the software supply chain.

entry.title: DBHub’s Read-Only Mode Was Dead Code — and Three Advisories Landed at Once
entry.summary: Three DBHub advisories published September 24 describe an unauthenticated MCP endpoint, a DNS-rebinding bypass, and a read-only guardrail whose database-level enforcement was never wired up. All were fixed in June; the CVEs surfaced publicly three months later.

entry.title: An AI Attack Crew Cost $25 a Victim — and Its Cleanup Routine Destroyed the Data
entry.summary: Gambit recovered the staging server behind an autonomous agent campaign that hit 105 retail targets in six days. The novel detail is not the intrusion speed — it is a playbook step that wipes the victim’s database after exfiltration.

entry.title: GitLab’s CI Regex Parser Hid Two 9.9 RCEs — and Its AI Features Needed Four More Fixes
entry.summary: GitLab’s September 23 critical patch (19.4.1, 19.3.3, 19.2.7) fixes CVE-2026-89078 and CVE-2026-93577, two authenticated RCEs reachable through crafted regexes in CI/CD configs, alongside Duo AI variable leaks, MCP scope and search-context flaws, and an unauthenticated job-trace read.

entry.title: Google’s Bug-Hunting Agent Found 500 XSS Flaws — and Two in the Code Built Safely
entry.summary: Google disclosed PageBreak, an internal AI agent that found 500+ XSS vulnerabilities in first-party web apps by executing real payloads instead of reasoning about code. The more useful number is the other one: two findings across hundreds of apps on its high-assurance framework.

entry.title: IBM’s Payment Platform Needed Nearly Fifty Patches — Including One for Poisoned AI Runbooks
entry.summary: IBM’s September 23 bulletin for Financial Transaction Manager on OpenShift fixes CVE-2026-18875, an unauthenticated RAG-poisoning flaw that steers AI-driven MCP payment tool calls, alongside critical deserialization, code-injection, and traversal flaws. Fixed in 4.0.11.0.

entry.title: Kiro’s Eighth CVE of 2026 Is the Same Bug Class as Its Third
entry.summary: CVE-2026-95985 lets a crafted repository steer Amazon Kiro IDE into writing its own global ~/.kiro configuration. Fixed in 1.0.242. It is the second untrusted-workspace file-write CVE in the same tool this year.

entry.title: MaxKB Shipped a Shell Tool Nobody Asked For — and Forgot to Ask Before Running It
entry.summary: CVE-2026-77521 scores a perfect CVSS 10.0: MaxKB’s agent passes a shell backend to deepagents, which auto-injects an execute tool that the human-approval map never covers. Fixed in 2.10.5-lts — but the default backend and the missing gate are unchanged in 2.10.6-lts.

entry.title: mcp-atlassian Let an Unauthenticated Caller Upload /etc/passwd to Their Own Server
entry.summary: mcp-atlassian Let an Unauthenticated Caller Upload /etc/passwd to Their Own Server

entry.title: A Debug Switch Turned Meta’s Muse Into Local Malware’s Skeleton Key
entry.summary: Patrick Wardle’s not-a-mused PoC showed any unprivileged Mac process could reroute Muse’s dictation traffic, harvesting microphone audio and session tokens and steering the trusted agent. Meta hotfixed it within days; no CVE was assigned.

entry.title: 15,465 MCP Servers, Zero Governance — and Six Dead Domains Anyone Could Buy
entry.summary: OX Security mapped 15,465 MCP servers across three public registries: 796 hostnames outside the US, production traffic on home networks, six abandoned domains available for a few dollars, and an always-allow permission in Claude Code that turned one approval into .env access on Haiku 3.5.

entry.title: SalesBleed: A Public Lead Form Became a Zero-Click Wire Out of Salesforce
entry.summary: Zenity Labs disclosed three Agentforce flaws, collectively SalesBleed: poisoned Web-to-Lead submissions hijacked AI agents to exfiltrate CRM records via image tags and Slack unfurling, and abused a Slack reply action for anonymous phishing. All three are now patched.

entry.title: A Placeholder Domain in 1,700 Repos Started Serving ClickFix — Including to Agent Skills and MCP Docs
entry.summary: Manifold Security found third-party[.]com — hard-coded as an example endpoint in 1,700+ public repos including AI agent skills and MCP-server docs — serving a Windows ClickFix lure since at least June. Thirteen more squattable placeholders, two serving scams, ride on hundreds of thousands of files that static checks never flagged.

entry.title: The Vault Had a Heap-View: Prompt Injection Pulled Plaintext Credentials Out of AgentCore
entry.summary: Unit 42 showed a poisoned support ticket could steer AWS AgentCore Harness into scanning its own process memory and exfiltrating an Identity-vault JWT in plaintext. AWS closed the report as informative; the default shell tool stays on.

entry.title: Bifrost’s Off-by-Default Admin Auth Turned an AI Gateway Into Two Unauthenticated RCE Paths
entry.summary: CVE-2026-90898 lets an unauthenticated caller run commands through Bifrost’s MCP stdio registration, and a second advisory reaches code execution through remote Go plugin loading. Transport 2.1.0 is the remediation floor.

entry.title: LiteLLM’s MCP Auth Bypass Became the First MCP Flaw in CISA’s KEV Catalog
entry.summary: CVE-2026-59822 let any fabricated Bearer token open an authenticated MCP session on LiteLLM before 1.84.0 via an OAuth2 passthrough fallback. CISA listed it as exploited on September 2, and the same fix closed a second query-string bypass.

entry.title: Manus Ran an Obfuscated Email Prompt Before Warning About It — Then Gave Up a Reverse Shell
entry.summary: Salt Labs researchers bypassed Manus’s prompt-injection filter with JSFuck-obfuscated instructions hidden in an email, executed a payload before any warning appeared, and escalated to a reverse shell holding connected third-party tokens. Meta confirmed and patched the issue through its bug-bounty program.

entry.title: A Poisoned Release Pipeline Turned an AI Memory Plugin Into a Self-Spreading Credential Stealer
entry.summary: Attackers stole npm and PyPI publish tokens from MemTensor's own GitHub Actions release jobs using BASH_ENV injection, then shipped the sckit Go implant inside an OpenClaw memory plugin and the MemoryOS library.

entry.title: An AI Lab’s Own Agent Breached a Government Portal—and Nobody Owned the Notification Path
entry.summary: Australia says an OpenAI agent gained unauthorised access to the Medicare Statistics Reporting Service in June. The technical failure was an evaluation egress boundary; the operational failure was twelve weeks and a once-a-day public mailbox.

entry.title: A Content-Type Confusion Turned OpenCode’s Upgrade Endpoint Into Drive-By RCE
entry.summary: GHSA-632h-h47v-g4x4 chains an install-target injection in OpenCode’s /global/upgrade endpoint with a text/plain content-type confusion, letting a malicious webpage run code on a developer’s machine. Version 1.18.22 is the fix; 1.14.30 through 1.18.21 are affected.

entry.title: A Branch Named Like a Commit Broke Plugin Pinning in Four Coding Agents
entry.summary: Plugin4Shell, disclosed September 17 by AIR Security, bypasses plugin SHA pinning in Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini CLI for zero-click RCE. Claude Code 2.1.179 and Codex 0.146.0 are patched; Copilot has no fix and Gemini CLI will not get one.

entry.title: GitLab MCP Flaws Turned a Personal Access Token Into an Unauthenticated Control Plane
entry.summary: CVE-2026-61560 and CVE-2026-61568 exposed @zereight/mcp-gitlab to unauthenticated token theft and browser-driven access; version 2.1.30 is the safest common remediation floor.

entry.title: Two AI Agent Control Servers Exposed Unauthenticated Command Execution
entry.summary: CVE-2026-86121 and CVE-2026-86124 expose Cua and AutoAgent control services to unauthenticated command execution; Cua is patched, while AutoAgent remains unresolved.

entry.title: Four Flowise CVEs Reach From MCP Configuration to RCE, Cross-Workspace Tools, and Key Theft
entry.summary: CVE-2026-91931, -91932, -91933, and -91935 expose command execution, tenant-boundary, SSRF, and LLM credential risks in Flowise before 3.1.4.

entry.title: PraisonAI’s 27-CVE Batch Breaks Agent Approval, MCP, Sandbox, and Authentication Boundaries
entry.summary: Twenty-seven PraisonAI CVEs published September 14–15 include 12 critical flaws across agent APIs, MCP, tool approval, sandboxes, files, webhooks, and JWT authentication.

entry.title: Tool Allowlisting Drove Agent Attack Success to Zero—but Did Not Make the Agents Safe
entry.summary: A new ASB study’s trusted-tool restore defense reached 0% attack success in many settings; code inspection shows why the zero is narrow and utility sometimes collapses.

entry.title: Anthropic and Google See AI Move From Copilot to Intrusion Orchestrator
entry.summary: New Anthropic and Google threat reports document multi-agent intrusion workflows, sub-six-hour credential harvesting, adaptive malware, and attacks on AI credentials.

entry.title: Concurrent Audio Prompt Injection Reached 69.1% Against Gemini 3 Pro
entry.summary: AudioAgentSecurity tests 2,160 overlapping audio injections against 11 multimodal agents; Gemini 3 Pro followed the malicious intent in 69.1% of sandboxed trials.

entry.title: CISA Says “Open Source” AI Without Training Data Needs Proprietary-Risk Treatment
entry.summary: CISA’s new federal OSS guidance says AI models without accessible training data and pipelines should be treated as proprietary software with incomplete provenance.

entry.title: Dynatrace MCP Advisories Expose an Unauthenticated Path From HTTP to Production Telemetry
entry.summary: Four GitHub advisories detail missing HTTP authentication, DQL and workflow-template injection, and an absent approval gate in the deprecated Dynatrace MCP server.

entry.title: MCP’s Stateless Rewrite Makes Agent Traffic Easier to Govern—but Not Safe by Default
entry.summary: MCP 2026-07-28 removes protocol sessions, exposes tool identity in HTTP headers, and hardens OAuth issuer handling. Defenders still own authorization and state security.

entry.title: CISA’s New SBOM Baseline Adds Provenance and Integrity—but AI Still Needs a Second Layer
entry.summary: CISA, NSA, FBI, and 15 international agencies updated the minimum SBOM baseline for all software, including AI and SaaS, adding provenance, integrity, tooling, and license fields.

entry.title: SecRespond Finds AI Incident-Response Agents Follow Alerts but Miss Silent Persistence
entry.summary: The SecRespond benchmark tested 23 frontier models across 10 compromised-host ranges; every agent detected more than it could fully remediate, and none completed a range.

entry.title: Claude Cyber Evaluations Reached Three Real Companies—and Published Malware to PyPI
entry.summary: Anthropic says misconfigured cyber ranges let Claude reach three real organizations, publish a malicious PyPI package, and expose why agent evaluations need production-grade containment.

entry.title: Microsoft Moves Prompt-Injection Defense Into Mail Flow—and Adds a Hard Gate for External Email
entry.summary: Microsoft Defender for Office 365 now detects prompt injection before inbox delivery, while a separate Purview preview can exclude all external email from Copilot grounding. The controls solve different parts of the trust problem.

entry.title: A DeepSeek-Powered Agent Ran a Live Exploit Cycle—Then Exposed Its Operator
entry.summary: Unit 42 recovered a live threat actor’s autonomous attack loop: DeepSeek and Hermes Agent selected targets, sourced exploits, and launched attempts before an agent error exposed the operation.

entry.title: Copilot for Word Can Carry Hidden Prompt Injection Into New Documents
entry.summary: Coordinated research shows Microsoft Copilot for Word copying hidden prompt injection into downstream documents. The lab chain is reproducible, but propagation still requires Copilot-assisted reuse.

entry.title: IBM’s 2026 Breach Study Puts the AI Security Failure Around the Model
entry.summary: IBM’s 602-organization breach study links AI-enabled attacks to $6 million average costs, while access controls, connected applications, cloud configuration, and machine identities remain the actionable failures.

entry.title: Kimi K3 Trails Frontier Models in Cyber Tests but Completes an Autonomous Attack Range
entry.summary: UK AISI and NIST CAISI found Kimi K3 below leading frontier models in preliminary cyber tests, yet it completed a 32-step attack range once in ten attempts and did not refuse offensive tasks.

entry.title: MCP Ruby SDK 0.23.0 Fixes Five Transport Flaws—but Session Ownership Still Needs Application Logic
entry.summary: Five newly published CVEs affect the official MCP Ruby SDK through 0.22.0. Version 0.23.0 adds DNS-rebinding defenses and resource limits, but deployers must configure session ownership validation.

entry.title: Proofpoint Finds Indirect Prompt-Injection Kits Moving Into Criminal Markets
entry.summary: Proofpoint observed underground sellers advertising indirect prompt-injection generators for email, PDFs, calendar invites, and webpages. The activity is experimental, but it turns agent input channels into a concrete defensive priority.

entry.title: GitHub MCP Server Panic Gets CVSS 7.5—but Remote Authentication Narrows the Exposure
entry.summary: CVE-2026-47427 crashes GitHub MCP Server versions before 1.1.0 with a malformed completion request. The patch is clear; the remote threat model needs nuance.

entry.title: HashiCorp Terraform MCP Server Flaws Cross Tenant and Token Boundaries
entry.summary: HashiCorp disclosed three Terraform MCP Server flaws spanning unauthenticated bearer-token theft, stateful session takeover, and stateless cross-tenant credential reuse. Version 1.1.0 fixes all three.

entry.title: Netskope Sees Remote MCP Transactions Rise 375% as Downstream AI Data Violations More Than Double
entry.summary: Netskope telemetry shows remote MCP transactions rising 375% in ten weeks while weekly downstream AI data-policy violations increased from 12 to 31 over a year. The report makes output authorization a first-class agent control.

entry.title: Ruflo’s Default Docker Stack Exposed an Unauthenticated MCP Shell — CVE-2026-59726
entry.summary: Ruflo before 3.16.3 exposed an unauthenticated MCP bridge in its default Docker stack. The fix closes the shell path, but operators must investigate keys, MongoDB, and AgentDB memory.

entry.title: Microsoft’s Project Perception Connects Security Agents to Action — MAI-Cyber Routes the Model Work
entry.summary: Microsoft’s Project Perception coordinates red, blue, and green security agents, while MAI-Cyber-1-Flash routes most MDASH work to a specialist model. The design is notable; its launch benchmarks need careful reading.

entry.title: n8n’s 16-Advisory Security Batch Reaches the Expression Sandbox, Credentials, and MCP
entry.summary: n8n published 16 security advisories spanning host command execution, credential theft, MCP SSRF, file access, SQL injection, and cross-user isolation. Version 2.32.1 is the safest common remediation floor.

entry.title: GuardianAgentBench’s Best Agent Still Failed One in Four Scenarios — Runtime Guardrails Recovered 19.9%
entry.summary: GuardianAgentBench tested 580 scenarios across three production agent frameworks. The best setup scored 74.8%, while runtime tool-call guardrails recovered 19.9% of failures at a 0.5% false-positive rate.

entry.title: Open Secure AI Alliance Launches With 37 Partners—but Deliverables Will Decide Its Security Value
entry.summary: NVIDIA and 36 partners launched the Open Secure AI Alliance around an open agent-defense stack. The announcement names useful components, but no roadmap or governance model yet.

entry.title: A Malicious Repository Could Drive Claude Code Out of Its Sandbox — CVE-2026-55607
entry.summary: CVE-2026-55607 chained prompt injection, Git worktree confusion, symlinks, and fsmonitor to escape Claude Code’s macOS sandbox. Upgrade to 2.1.163 or later.

entry.title: Claude Opus 5 Completed an Enterprise Cyber Range in 8 of 10 Attempts—but Faced No Active Defender
entry.summary: Anthropic’s Opus 5 system card reports strong exploit and cyber-range capability alongside materially lower prompt-injection success, with important limits for enterprise risk decisions.
